title: I handed Claude the code from a game I made 20 years ago to see how much I could improve it
author: Quick-Somewhere-918
selftext:
About 20 years ago, I made a little multiplayer bomb game called Blaster Bastards. The source code has been sitting around ever since, and I wanted to see if I could revive the old game and how much I could improve it using modern AI tools.

https://preview.redd.it/5zpb7jah6puh1.png?width=1020&format=png&auto=webp&s=bd979076ca98a9298b1c7a07604854b8a84cb354

I started with the original source code and worked my way through the game, improving the graphics, gameplay, and adding new features along the way.

Here's what I ended up using:

* **Claude Opus 5.5** — Coding, gameplay improvements, and computer-controlled opponents.
* **GPT-6** — New graphics, characters, and game assets.
* **Suno** — New music.

https://preview.redd.it/wlim8coi6puh1.png?width=1600&format=png&auto=webp&s=4c889b9d09c7bbb4ca834591c03565b22a33af43

It's fun to see how easy it is to try out new ideas without spending hours implementing them. I could simply describe what I wanted, test the result, make adjustments, and move on to the next idea.

I eventually asked Claude to make the computer opponents smarter, then challenged myself to beat them. That was an interesting experience! 😂

I've been programming for decades, but I find myself enjoying the creative and architectural side much more than actually writing code these days. AI lets me focus on those parts while progressing much faster.

It took me around 1 week, and it is actually fun to play the game now 😀

I documented the process and the final gameplay in a video if anyone is interested:  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5V5N4kxwKc](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5V5N4kxwKc)

I've also made the finished game available for free for Windows and Mac.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body:
Omg AI stole bomber, omg you should be ashamed blah blah… 

Just kidding, but yeah with AI it is very simple to just test things out and experiment, one of the benefits of AI. In some cases I would experiment with shaders so much that I would spend 30-40% of weekly limits just to see “how it would look like” even with no real plans to use them for example mockup of the water on the left and me spending 50% weekly limit of 200$ claude plan on the right. I never ended using it, and abandoned the shader but wanted to see how good can it get, it did it in just few hours 🫣

replies.author: Quick-Somewhere-918
replies.body:
Hehe, yeah, it's easy to end up in an endless loop of improvements. 😁

For me, this was a bit of a side project compared to what I usually do, but it was pretty fun, so I might try the same thing with some of my other old games at some point.

Nice shaders, btw! :)

replies.author: Kalaminator
replies.body:
I mean, there are people literally posting cloned games made in 4 prompts, and think they did something cool while lacking common sense, analytical and thinking and self awareness.

This post is totally different to what I mentioned before. I'm all in on people taking on an existing concept or game and improving, adding extra stuff and making changes with intention and purpose, it doesn't have to be something crazy. Specially the fact that it was one of his old projects, this is very cool.

replies.author: Quick-Somewhere-918
replies.body:
Thanks! 😁 I have so many old, dusty projects lying around, and bringing one of them back to life was a lot of fun.

Graphics have never been my strong suit, so being able to use AI for that helps a lot. Despite the occasional frustration when no matter how you word the prompt, it just refuses to produce the result you're looking for! 🤣
